hunks.baseline: Despite my boast that we’d cut the remaining time down to two days, reality was cold. The farther we ventured into the wilderness to avoid drawing attention, the more time we inevitably lost.
hunks.sol: Despite my boast that we’d cut the remaining time down to two days, reality was less accommodating. The deeper we went to avoid drawing attention, the more time we lost.

hunks.baseline: “We’re not the only ones on the move. We have to push ourselves and get in their way before they reach their destination.”
hunks.sol: “We’re not the only ones on the move. We have to push ourselves hard enough to get ahead of them.”

hunks.baseline: If we’d picked up some information, then so had our opponents.
hunks.sol: If we’d learned something, our opponents might have learned something, too.

hunks.baseline: Wherever they were headed, they were still within the Great Nation’s territory. Eyes and ears were everywhere, and there had been countless variables from the start. There was only one way to minimize them.
hunks.sol: Wherever we went, we were still within the Great Nation’s territory. With eyes and ears everywhere, there had been countless variables from the start. There was only one way to minimize them.

hunks.baseline: It was insane to try to cross half the continent in a little over half a month.
hunks.sol: We were trying to cross half the continent in a little over half a month. It was insane.

hunks.baseline: “If you want to rest, rest. I’m not being sarcastic or trying to hint at anything. If you think you can’t go on, drop out. It’ll be better for all of us.”
hunks.sol: “If you want to rest, rest. I’m not being sarcastic or hinting at anything. If you think you can’t go on, drop out. It’ll be better for all of us.”

hunks.baseline: No—neither did anyone else.
hunks.sol: Neither did anyone else.

hunks.baseline: Instead of complaining, they held their tongues and kept moving.
hunks.sol: They held their tongues instead of complaining, and we kept moving.

hunks.baseline: The vast continent’s climate and terrain varied a little from one region to the next.
hunks.sol: The vast continent’s climate and terrain varied from one region to the next.

hunks.baseline: The midday heat in Hubei was like a blast furnace, while the night wind in Anhui cut like a cold blade.
hunks.sol: The midday heat in Hubei was like a blast furnace, while a chilly wind cut through the nights in Anhui.

hunks.baseline: One day, after a storm swept through, some of the party finally collapsed, unable to overcome their exhaustion.
hunks.sol: One day, after wind and rain had swept through, some of the party collapsed from exhaustion.

hunks.baseline: “Young Hero Jin, I understand how important this matter is, but… we can’t go on any longer.”
hunks.sol: “Young Hero Jin, I understand how important this is, but… they can’t go on.”

hunks.baseline: At the Divine Physician’s words, spoken after watching the members grow exhausted by the day, I gave him a short reply.
hunks.sol: The Divine Physician had watched the others wear themselves down. I gave him a short answer.

hunks.baseline: “We’ll set out again after fifteen minutes.”
hunks.sol: “We’ll rest for fifteen minutes, then set out again.”

hunks.baseline: I carried Hyuk Mujin on my back, and Jeok Cheongang did the same with Ju Hwaran.
hunks.sol: I carried Hyuk Mujin on my back, and Jeok Cheongang carried Ju Hwaran.

hunks.baseline: Both of them refused at first, but this time I wouldn’t budge. It was obvious at a glance that neither of them was in any condition to be called well, even as a joke.
hunks.sol: Both refused at first, but this time I wouldn’t budge. One look told me they were in no condition to say they were fine, even as a joke.

hunks.baseline: *Of course they’re exhausted. We’ve been moving until our internal energy and stamina were completely spent.*
hunks.sol: *Of course they’re exhausted. We’ve been moving until their internal energy and stamina were spent.*

hunks.baseline: And though his title was the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang was a man of cold disposition. For some reason, he felt sorry for Ju Hwaran, who was burning up from head to toe despite the Divine Physician’s treatment.
hunks.sol: And despite his title of Fire King, Jeok Cheongang had a cold disposition. Yet he seemed to feel sorry for Ju Hwaran, who was burning up with fever despite the Divine Physician’s treatment.

hunks.baseline: “Was this really necessary? We could—”
hunks.sol: “Is this really necessary? We could—”

hunks.baseline: The war had already begun, and upheaval lurked all around us.
hunks.sol: The war had already begun, and upheaval lurked on every side.

hunks.baseline: Catastrophes so terrible and vast that no one had ever experienced anything like them.
hunks.sol: Catastrophes more terrible and vast than anything anyone had ever faced.

hunks.baseline: To survive the war against Dark Heaven, all of us had to grow stronger—not just me. A blade hammered and tempered countless times won’t break even when it strikes a rock.
hunks.sol: To survive the war against Dark Heaven, all of us had to grow stronger—not just me. A blade hammered and tempered countless times wouldn’t break when it struck a rock.

hunks.baseline: And Jeok Cheongang was one of the very few people who understood the meaning of my words better than anyone.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang was one of the very few people who understood what I meant better than anyone.

hunks.baseline: He, too, had been remade through bone-deep effort and hardship. In the end, he’d become a peerless blade that cut through countless rocks blocking his way.
hunks.sol: He, too, had been remade through grueling effort and hardship. In the end, he’d become a fine blade that cut through the countless rocks in his path.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang slowly repeated the words he’d heard from me, then gave a dry chuckle.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang slowly repeated my words, then gave a dry chuckle.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang shook his head at my answer.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang shook his head.

hunks.baseline: “Miss Ju wanted it. I respected her wishes. If she were in enough pain to actually die, I’d have stopped her myself.”
hunks.sol: “Young Lady Ju wanted this. I respected her wishes. If she’d been in so much pain she might actually die, I’d have stopped her myself.”

hunks.baseline: “Cut the crap. Anyway, your idea might be right, but I can be sure of one thing.”
hunks.sol: “Cut the crap. Your thinking may be right, but there’s one thing I’m sure of.”

hunks.baseline: “Yes? What?”
hunks.sol: “What’s that?”

hunks.baseline: “This old man guarantees you’ll never find a partner before you die.”
hunks.sol: “This old man guarantees you’ll never find a partner as long as you live.”

hunks.baseline: “Hey, why are you suddenly bringing that up?”
hunks.sol: “Where did that come from?”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang suddenly landed a brutal verbal blow, then darted away like the wind. As I watched his back, I noticed my view gradually growing brighter and raised my head.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang dealt that brutal blow out of nowhere and darted away like the wind. As I watched him go, I noticed the world growing brighter and raised my head.

hunks.baseline: I gathered my internal energy and pushed off the ground. Stepping onto the branch of the nearest great tree, I sprang up into its crown. At last, I saw a glow spreading in the distance.
hunks.sol: I gathered my internal energy and pushed off the ground. Stepping onto a branch of the nearest great tree, I sprang up above it. At last, I saw the light spreading in the distance.

hunks.baseline: It was the dawn light.
hunks.sol: Dawn.

hunks.baseline: The eleventh dawn I’d seen, one each day since we’d left the Sichuan Tang Clan.
hunks.sol: The eleventh dawn I’d seen since we’d left the Sichuan Tang Clan.

hunks.baseline: But the reason that light heralding a new morning felt especially welcome today was something coming into view beyond the grass and streams stretching all around us.
hunks.sol: But what made the light of this new morning so welcome was something coming into view beyond the grass and streams that surrounded us.

hunks.baseline: A faint exclamation rang in my ears.
hunks.sol: A faint exclamation sounded by my ear.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin, slung over my back, asked in a voice that sounded half dead,

hunks.baseline: “C-Captain. Where are we? What’s that?”
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin, still on my back, asked in a half-dead voice, “C-Captain. Where are we? What’s that?”

hunks.baseline: Then, loud enough for everyone below the tree to hear, I answered:
hunks.sol: Then I answered loudly enough for everyone below the tree to hear.

hunks.baseline: Each of them was a fine warrior and herdsman. They worshiped heaven and earth and were close companions to hawks and horses, but they were not good rulers.
hunks.sol: Each was a fine warrior and herdsman. They worshiped heaven and earth and were close companions to hawks and horses, but they were not good rulers.

hunks.baseline: There had been a great conqueror who was both hero and devil, destined to remain a legend to the very end. There had also been a wise ruler who strengthened the empire from within and cared for his subjects and people.
hunks.sol: There had been a great conqueror, both hero and devil, who remained a legend to the very end. There had also been a wise ruler who strengthened the empire from within and cared for his subjects.

hunks.baseline: But when that age drew to a close, all that remained were horrific famine, corruption, and countless red flags fluttering in the wind.
hunks.sol: But at the end of that age, all that remained were terrible famine, corruption, and countless red flags fluttering in the wind.

hunks.baseline: An age of war began. Figures wearing blood-red flags and headscarves rose like wildfires from every direction and swept across the continent.
hunks.sol: An age of war began. People with blood-red flags and headscarves rose like wildfire on every side and swept across the continent.

hunks.baseline: The world called them the Red Turban Bandits. They wanted to be called the Red Turban Army, but in truth, the former name suited them better.
hunks.sol: The world called them the Red Turbans—bandits. They wanted to be called the Red Turban Army, but the world’s judgment was closer to the truth.

hunks.baseline: Bandits who stole grain and treasure to fill their empty stomachs.
hunks.sol: Bandits who stole grain and valuables to fill their empty stomachs.

hunks.baseline: *“How can the blood of kings, nobles, generals, and ministers be any different from anyone else’s?”*
hunks.sol: *“Are kings and generals born of some different blood?”*

hunks.baseline: Even if they were shabby on the outside, did that mean their insides had to be small and shabby, too?
hunks.sol: They might have been shabby on the outside, but did that mean there was nothing great within them?

hunks.baseline: Just as one hero had done at the end of that long age of war, at last grasping all under heaven.
hunks.sol: Just as one hero had done at the end of that long age of war, when he finally seized all under heaven.

hunks.baseline: *“Your Majesty, please ascend the throne!”*
hunks.sol: *“My king, please ascend the imperial throne!”*

hunks.baseline: Born the son of a poor farmer, he had wandered the land as a mendicant monk. Now he held all under heaven in his hands and occupied the highest position of all, with countless subjects and commoners beneath him.
hunks.sol: Born the son of a poor farmer, he had wandered the land as a mendicant monk. Now he held all under heaven in his hands and stood above everyone, with countless officials and commoners beneath him.

hunks.baseline: But even after many years had passed and one of his own children inherited the throne, nothing changed.
hunks.sol: But even after many years had passed and one of his children inherited the throne, nothing changed.

hunks.baseline: *“Hey, you filthy beggar!”*
hunks.sol: *“Hey, you beggar brat!”*

hunks.baseline: Filthy beggar.
hunks.sol: Beggar brat.

hunks.baseline: It was one of the things he’d heard most often in his life. Even now, decades later, the memory was etched clearly into his mind.
hunks.sol: It was one of the things he’d heard most often in his life. Even now, decades later, that moment was etched clearly into his mind.

hunks.baseline: So clearly that it appeared without fail whenever he had a nightmare like this one.
hunks.sol: It appeared without fail whenever he had a nightmare like this one.

hunks.baseline: Hong Jin abruptly woke from his sleep and blinked. Then he respectfully bowed his head to the boy watching him in silence.
hunks.sol: Hong Jin woke with a start and blinked. Then he respectfully bowed his head to the boy who had been watching him in silence.

hunks.baseline: “I dared to fall into a dream before Your Highness. Please forgive your unfaithful servant.”
hunks.sol: “I dared to dream in Your Highness’s presence. Please forgive your unfaithful servant.”

hunks.baseline: “Forgive you? There’s no need.”
hunks.sol: “Forgive you? Don’t be absurd.”

hunks.baseline: The boy, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao, replied.
hunks.sol: The boy was Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao.

hunks.baseline: His composure and dignified voice were hard to believe in someone who wasn’t even midway through his teens.
hunks.sol: His composure and dignified voice were hard to believe in someone not yet in his midteens.

hunks.baseline: The young prince, taller and more solidly built than most boys his age, continued speaking to his servant.
hunks.sol: The young prince, much taller and more solidly built than most boys his age, continued speaking to his servant.

hunks.baseline: “But set aside any needless worry. What you’re afraid of will never happen.”
hunks.sol: “But set aside your worries. What you fear will never happen.”

hunks.baseline: But as he stared at the floor of the slowly moving carriage, his gaze held both pride in the young prince and a hint of bitterness.
hunks.sol: Yet as he looked down at the floor of the slowly moving carriage, he felt both pride in the young prince and bitterness.

hunks.baseline: Hong Jin forced down the voice rising deep in his heart.
hunks.sol: Hong Jin forced down the words rising in his heart.

hunks.baseline: His master, Prince Shangshan, had been an intelligent, mature boy from a young age. But he was far too young to understand the cruelty of the world.
hunks.sol: His master, Prince Shangshan, had been intelligent and mature from a young age. But he was far too young to understand the cruelty of the world.

hunks.baseline: Even now, as they traveled toward the imperial capital surrounded by the Embroidered Uniform Guard as if he were a prisoner being taken away, he still had unwavering faith in his only blood relative.
hunks.sol: Even now, surrounded by the Embroidered Uniform Guard and bound for the Imperial Capital as though he were a prisoner under escort, he still had unwavering faith in his only blood relative.

hunks.baseline: But Hong Jin did not.
hunks.sol: Hong Jin did not.

hunks.baseline: *You already have all under heaven. What more could you possibly want, Your Majesty?*
hunks.sol: *You already have all under heaven. What more could you possibly want, Emperor?*

hunks.baseline: In the pitch-darkness, memories surfaced. Sounds returned.
hunks.sol: In the darkness, memories surfaced. Sounds returned.

hunks.baseline: Those days when the blood never dried. Days of purges when hundreds had their limbs torn off and died, and thousands were beheaded and displayed.
hunks.sol: The days when the blood never dried. The days of purges, when hundreds died with their limbs torn from their bodies and thousands were beheaded, their heads put on display.

hunks.baseline: *“Bao. I entrust that child to you.”*
hunks.sol: *“Bao. Look after that child.”*

hunks.baseline: Hong Jin opened his eyes at a small jolt that traveled through the carriage. He turned to look beside him and saw someone’s profile through a narrow gap in the window.
hunks.sol: A small jolt ran through the carriage. Hong Jin opened his eyes, turned, and saw someone’s profile through a gap in the window.

hunks.baseline: At Hong Jin’s low question, the man beside the carriage, dressed in shabby martial robes ill-suited to the name Embroidered Uniform Guard, replied,
hunks.sol: At Hong Jin’s low question, the man beside the carriage replied. He wore shabby martial robes that hardly suited the name Embroidered Uniform Guard.

hunks.baseline: His voice was blunt, without even the hint of emotion. But Hong Jin sensed the cold blade lurking beneath it.
hunks.sol: His voice was blunt, devoid of emotion. But Hong Jin sensed a cold blade beneath it.

hunks.baseline: A feeling both unfamiliar and familiar.
hunks.sol: A feeling both strange and familiar.

hunks.baseline: Just like the Embroidered Uniform Guard now, Hong Jin had once served as the late Emperor’s hands and feet. The sensation brought back something familiar that he hadn’t felt in over a decade.
hunks.sol: Hong Jin had once served as the late Emperor’s hands and feet, just as the Embroidered Uniform Guard did now. The man’s voice brought back a sensation he hadn’t felt in over a decade.

hunks.baseline: Along with a hint of puzzlement.
hunks.sol: And with it came a question.

hunks.baseline: This covert procession had already entered Jiangsu, and the Embroidered Uniform Guard had no reason to stop. They were people who would gladly give their lives to carry out the Emperor’s orders.
hunks.sol: The covert procession had already entered Jiangsu, and the Embroidered Uniform Guard had no reason to stop. They would give their lives to carry out an imperial order.

hunks.baseline: Hong Jin quietly sharpened his senses. He might not be skilled enough to have established his own school, but he had still learned martial arts.
hunks.sol: Hong Jin quietly sharpened his senses. He might not have mastered martial arts to the point of founding his own school, but he had learned them.

hunks.baseline: Thankfully, the guards seemed to judge that the matter wasn’t serious enough to require Sound Transmission. Their conversation drifted through the gap in the window.
hunks.sol: Fortunately, the guards seemed to decide the matter didn’t warrant Sound Transmission. Their conversation drifted through the gap in the window.

hunks.baseline: “According to the scouts, there’s an unidentified corpse about three hundred zhang ahead…”
hunks.sol: “According to the scouts, there’s an unidentified body about three hundred zhang ahead…”

hunks.baseline: “We didn’t approach in case it was a trap, but there don’t seem to be any obvious wounds…”
hunks.sol: “They didn’t get close in case it was a trap, but they couldn’t see any obvious wounds…”

hunks.baseline: The murmuring conversation abruptly stopped. After a brief pause, the carriage started moving again.
hunks.sol: The murmured conversation cut off. After its brief halt, the carriage began to move again.

hunks.sol: Listening to the soft sound of hooves, Hong Jin thought, *An unidentified body.*

hunks.baseline: *An unidentified corpse.*
It wasn’t that strange. The continent was vast, and there were people begging their way across it everywhere. Not even Jiangsu, so close to the imperial capital, was an exception.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t so strange. The continent was vast, and people wandered its roads begging for food. Even Jiangsu, so close to the Imperial Capital, was no exception.

hunks.baseline: But why?
Why did one man’s name suddenly come to mind at this very moment?
hunks.sol: But why did one man’s name come to mind now?

hunks.baseline: And why did an inexplicable hope well up in one corner of his heart?
hunks.sol: And why did hope suddenly rise in his chest?

hunks.baseline: Hong Jin had just lifted his head when—
hunks.sol: Hong Jin lifted his head.

hunks.baseline: With one of the Embroidered Uniform Guard’s men murmuring the words, a familiar voice Hong Jin had heard somewhere reached his ears.
hunks.sol: One of the Embroidered Uniform Guard had muttered the words. Then a voice Hong Jin recognized reached his ears.

hunks.baseline: At that moment, Hong Jin burst out laughing, briefly forgetting that the young prince was right in front of him.
hunks.sol: For a moment, Hong Jin forgot the young prince was right in front of him and burst out laughing.
